note: Shenzhen and Dongguan landmark and site targets for the Greater Bay map (City Brush, gbareal; see gba/BRIEF.md). lat/lon = the centroid of the named OSM footprint (osm = its id: w way, r relation; towers given by their plot are anchored on the tallest building of this build inside it, the plot kept under plot). h = verified overall height (m) or null; h_osm = OSM height / levels; h_app = this build's height. r = suggested model radius (m). region = hk / sz / dg / other (context) at the anchor. existing = a key already modelled in a Hong Kong module (count it, do not duplicate it). hero = a recognisable detailed replica. Names: zh Simplified, en English.

szcbd.existing: hk/shenzhen/shenzhen.js (v37 skyline-level model, ~4 kB per tower): UPGRADE to the Hong Kong standard under the same key

szcbd.notes: OMA 2013: square glass tower with the huge "raised podium" platform cantilevered about 36 m above the ground
szcbd.existing: hk/hkx_nt/hkx_nt.js (v38, Hong Kong standard): keep; check it in situ on this map (ground, decks) and only fix what is wrong

szcbd.notes: BIG 2017: two towers (north 218 m architectural, 219.1 m tip; south 110 m) whose facades are a pleated white skin folding open and closed in long vertical waves (the folds shade the glass); joined by a podium
2021, 70 floors: slender glass office tower on Shennan Road at the CBD, the second tallest in Futian
2010: four towers on one plot south of Ping An; Tower 1 280 m (60 floors), Tower 2 250 m; dark glass with vertical fins
1998, 48 floors: tower on Shennan Road at the CBD with a tall open crown frame over the roof
2001, 53 floors: the bank's former headquarters on Shennan Road (no name or logo on the model)
2011 (formerly Lvjing Plaza): tower A 273 m, 56 floors, with its lower twin towers on Shennan Road at Chegongmiao
North of Lianhuashan: Tower 1 388.1 m (2020), Tower 2 299.3 m (2017), over a terraced "town" podium of low blocks and roof gardens
At the south end of the CBD axis (2004): a long low hall under a vast flat roof on a grid of slender columns, glazed all round; the main hall and its big portico face the Civic Center

Metro interchange (2022) at Shennan / Caitian Road: underground, but famous for its giant glazed oculus ("Shenzhen Eye") at street level; model the oculus, its plaza and entrances (anchor = the station footprint: find the oculus in the refs)

szcivic.notes: Lee/Timchula: the city hall under one 486 m long, 154 m wide curved "wing" roof (truss 1998, cladding 2004) over a central block and two side wings; part of the Shenzhen Museum inside; the axis of the CBD
Arata Isozaki (Shenzhen Cultural Center, with the Concert Hall): long glass hall with a curved curtain wall over a stone base on Fuzhong Road
Arata Isozaki, 2007: 1 800-seat vineyard hall in a glass box; the golden tree-like columns in the glazed foyer; joined to the Library

szcivic.zh: 深圳市当代艺术与城市规划馆
szcivic.en: Museum of Contemporary Art and Planning Exhibition (MOCAPE)
szcivic.notes: Coop Himmelb(l)au 2016: a big flat box wrapped in a perforated metal skin with a free-form glazed "cloud" cut into it and the plaza under it; north of the Civic Center
Children's cultural centre on the axis next to MOCAPE: glass volumes and a tower-like science hall
Long low bookstore mall on the central axis between the Civic Center and Lianhuashan, under a long roof with a glazed central street
Hill park at the north end of the axis: the bronze Deng Xiaoping statue (2000) on the summit plaza looking south over the CBD, the kite lawn, the lake (site)
Long park along the Futian River between Futian and Luohu: lawns, the river, footbridges, trees (site)
Boundary control point to Lok Ma Chau Spur Line (2007): long glass-and-steel hall over the Shenzhen River approach and the footbridge
The new Huanggang control point building (rebuilt in the 2020s, co-location with Hong Kong); check its state in photos and the refs (anchor = the OSM footprint)
Mangroves and boardwalks on the Shenzhen Bay shore beside the Futian reserve, the Hong Kong skyline of Mai Po across the water (site)

szluohu.notes: Luohu 2011, 100 floors: slender tower with a softly bulging, curved profile (wider in the middle), the curved glass crown; vertical fins
szluohu.existing: hk/shenzhen/shenzhen.js (v37 skyline-level model, ~4 kB per tower): UPGRADE to the Hong Kong standard under the same key

szluohu.notes: 1996, 69 floors: early all-steel supertall; very slim slab with rounded ends, green-blue glass, a stepped top with the two tall masts; next to KK100
1985, 50 floors: the "Shenzhen speed" tower; cylindrical revolving restaurant on floors 48-49 and a helipad on top; tallest in China 1985-87
2000, 71 floors: octagonal grey-glass tower over the Huaqiangbei electronics market podium (its rooftop masts since removed)
2022, 70 floors: slim tower north of the railway in Luohu (Caiwuwei / Hubei)
1989 theatre on Shennan Road at the foot of Diwang: a glass-walled hall under a big flat roof slab (one of the city's first cultural buildings)
Main station of the old Guangzhou-Kowloon line beside Lo Wu: long concourse with a big roof, the square in front, the Luohu Commercial City next door
Joint inspection building over the Shenzhen River by the railway station, the footbridge to Lo Wu (Hong Kong)
The old market town of Shenzhen: pedestrian lanes, arcades, the old Siwei Tower area; paving, lamps, trees (site; no shop signs)

The electronics market street: Huaqiang North Road, pedestrianised over the metro (2017), with its malls on both sides (site: paving, canopies, trees, lamps; no signs). Anchor = a point on the road, uncertain: take the street from the refs

szluohu.zh: 深圳博物馆古代艺术馆
szluohu.notes: The 1988 museum building in Lizhi Park's corner on Shennan Road: a low pavilion block with a big overhanging roof

szhouhai.notes: NBBJ 2017: two towers (50 and 41 floors) joined by three bridging "links" at low, middle and high levels; glass with sun-shade fins (no logo)

Tower 7 (2018, 71 floors), the tallest of the One Shenzhen Bay group facing the bay, with a lit crown

szhouhai.en: Shenzhen Bay Innovation and Technology Centre

szhouhai.zh: 招商银行全球总部大厦

szshekou.notes: Shekou plaza round the landlocked cruise liner Minghua (ex-Ancerville, built 1962 at Saint-Nazaire, 168 m x 22 m, at Shekou since 1983): white hull, the funnel; the fountain plaza and lanes round it. The ship is not an OSM footprint: find it in the refs / photos

szshekou.zh: 海上世界文化艺术中心

Ferry / cruise terminal at Prince Bay: long wavy-roofed hall on the shore with the gangways
Temple of the sea goddess at Chiwan (rebuilt in the Ming / Qing style): halls stepping up the hill axis, red walls, glazed roofs, the archway and stone steps

szshekou.en: Tomb of the Last Song Emperor

Waterfront park with the "Qianhai Stone" boulder (the area's symbol) facing the Qianhai towers (site)

szshekou.en: Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Youth Innovation Hub

Container port at Shekou / Chiwan: the quay cranes along the berths, the stacks, the gantries (site: cranes are the point)

Miniature China (Great Wall, palaces, pagodas at reduced scale) and the folk-culture village of ethnic houses (site)
Amusement park in OCT: roller coasters, the drop tower, the lake (site: rides as structures, no brand imagery)

2020, 60 floors: diamond (rhombus) footprint turned to limit shading; glass with vertical fins
National art museum (1997): low white stone-and-glass block with a courtyard and pool, Lingnan modernism
Converted 1980s factory blocks (the original OCT industrial area): concrete frames, brick, the vines and courtyards (site)
Zoo in Xili under the hills: drive-through enclosures, pavilions, paths (site; animals optional, no mascots)

szoct.en: Southern University of Science and Technology
szoct.notes: Campus in Xili round the hills and lake: the library, the white teaching blocks and the new research towers (site)

szoct.en: Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen (University Town)

The X-shaped satellite concourse north of T3 (its piers radiating from a central hall), glazed

Opened 18 Apr 2021 at OH Bay (Qianhai Bay): 128 m high, 113.3 m diameter, 28 cabins on a cantilevered wheel; LED-lit rim at night

szbaoan.en: Eyes of the GBA (Bay Area Book City)
szbaoan.notes: Two low curved halls (north and south) facing OH Bay round a central opening, the "eye"; green roofs

sznorth.notes: High-speed hub (HSR 26 Dec 2011): the big roof over the tracks; metro Lines 4 and 6 run elevated through the east square under the roof; the elevated passage at the 9 m level
Longhua cultural district by the North Station: with the Library North Branch (Second Library) one pair of white buildings round a plaza
The second city library next to the new Art Museum: a long white block with deep vertical fins

Zaha Hadid Architects (with BIAD), opened 1 May 2025, Guangming: one sweeping rounded "spaceship" volume facing the city, stepping down into terraces over the Science Park on its west side; stainless-steel panels anodised from deep blue to greys
Restored market street of arcaded shophouses (qilou) and the old watch towers on the Guanlan River (site)
The painters' village in Longgang: lanes of studios and galleries with paintings on the walls (no copies of real artworks needed), the art museum (site)
2023 twin towers (71 floors each) at Bantian, Longgang: two identical towers side by side (west w1190193566 = anchor, east w1190193567; OSM says 369 m), lit crowns

gmp, 2011 Summer Universiade: stadium (60 334 seats), arena (18 000) and natatorium (3 000), each wrapped in a faceted "crystal" shell of triangular translucent panels on a steel lattice, round a lake (site)

sznorth.en: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
sznorth.notes: Campus (2014) on the hills next to the Universiade Centre: the lower and upper campuses, red-brick and stone blocks, the library (site)
Large Qing Hakka walled house in Longgang: square enclosure with corner watch towers, rows of halls round courtyards, grey walls and tiled roofs; the Hakka folk museum
Qing Hakka walled compound in Pingshan: rectangular, moat in front, corner towers, the ancestral hall axis, grey roofs
Theatre in Pingshan centre. Anchor uncertain: the OSM object of that name is the planted area round it; find the building in the refs

szeast.notes: Transmission tower on Small Wutong above Luohu, the landmark on the ridge seen from the city (height unverified: take it from photos)
The highest peak of Shenzhen, 943.7 m (the app's 70 m grid reads lower): the summit rocks, the paths and the summit marker (site; no text)

Chan temple (1985-1992) at the foot of Wutong Shan in the Fairy Lake garden: about forty buildings up the hill axis, the mountain gate, the Hall of the Four Heavenly Kings, the Mahavira Hall, the bell and drum towers; yellow walls, glazed roofs
The botanical garden round Fairy Lake under Wutong Shan: the lake, glasshouses, pavilions (site)
The reservoir that stores the Dongjiang water for Shenzhen and Hong Kong: the dam and its spillway, the lake shore (site: the dam)
One of the world's biggest container ports: the long quays with rows of quay cranes, the stacks and the mountains behind (site)
The border street in Sha Tau Kok: one side Shenzhen, one side Hong Kong (1899 border line); the warning bell monument, the boundary stones, the low shops (site). Anchor = the warning-bell node

Steven Holl 2009, the "horizontal skyscraper": a long bent bar floating over a tropical garden on eight cores up to 50 m apart, under the 35 m height limit; perforated louvred facade; green roof (the OSM area is tagged school: check)
The public beach of Yantian: the sand, the promenade, palms, the sculptures (site)

szeast.zh: 东部华侨城茵特拉根小镇
szeast.notes: Mountain resort above Dameisha: the Swiss-style town square, the lake and the lodges (site: architecture only, no signage)
Ming coastal fortress (1394) against pirates: the square walled town with its gates, the lanes of Qing houses and the generals' mansions (site)
Beach village of guesthouses south of the fortress on Dapeng Bay: colourful low houses, the beach (site)

dgcity.notes: The city hall at the north end of the central square: a vast symmetric block with a colonnade and a big flat roof, facing the axis
The long axis of lawns, fountains and trees between the City Hall and the theatre / library / museum cluster (site)
The city theatre on the central square: a shell-like roof form over the glass foyer (named after the city flower, the yulan)
The main city library on the central square beside the Yulan theatre: glass-and-stone block with a big atrium
The museum site on the central square (check in photos whether it is open or under construction; the old museum is in Guancheng, b:w520439671)
The exhibition hall on the central square axis

dgcity.zh: 环球经贸中心（台商大厦）
dgcity.notes: 2013, 68 floors (Taiwan Business Association tower / Global Trade Plaza) on Dongguan Avenue by the central square
T2 422.6 m, 96 floors (opened 2021), the tallest in Dongguan, with its shorter sister towers on the mall podium
One of the four great Lingnan gardens (1850, Zhang Jingxiu): grey-brick pavilions, corridors and the tall look-out pavilion, ponds (site)
The surviving west gate of the old walled city of Dongguan (Ming): the brick-and-stone gate base with its tiled gate tower
Hill park on Huangqi Shan east of the centre: the paths, the pavilions and the giant red lantern on the summit (find it in the refs / photos) (site)

dghumen.notes: Opened 9 June 1997: suspension bridge, 888 m main span (navigation clearance 60 m) across the Pearl River from Humen (Dongguan) to Nansha; the auxiliary channel bridge is a concrete rigid frame 150 + 270 + 150 m (clearance 40 m); main bridge 4.588 km. Write a deck fix (the generic deck rule is far too low)
Opened 2 April 2019 (the second Humen bridge, Shatian in Dongguan to Nansha): suspension bridge with a 1 688 m main span. Deck fix needed
The western suspension span of the Nansha Bridge (1 200 m main span), on the Guangzhou side (context region)

dghumen.en: Opium War Museum and the Opium Destruction Pools

Qing battery on Weiyuan Island by the Humen Bridge: the long curved granite gun wall with embrasures facing the river
Museum on Weiyuan Island at the foot of the Humen Bridge: the low halls, the sculpture plaza
Qing fort on the Shajiao headland at the river mouth: batteries and walls on the hill. Point anchor: find it in the refs
High-speed station (Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong line, 2011): long roof over the elevated platforms

dghumen.zh: 广东现代国际展览中心

Large Lingnan-style garden at Daojiao: lakes, bridges, pavilions and corridors (site)

dgsongshan.zh: 东莞理工学院（松山湖校区）

Forest park in Zhangmutou with the large white stone Guanyin statue on the summit terrace and the temple halls (anchor = the park: find the statue in the refs; height unverified)
Ming-Qing village in Chashan: the long pond with ancestral halls on both banks, grey-brick houses, watch towers (site)
